text:
alex: quick heads-up — i'm going to start the v2 rollout for /generate in eu-west in ~30m. small shard groups (10% traffic) to start. please do not pin any tenants until we get the first telemetry window.

priya: noted. are we using the sticky-shard fallback or the header-based routing for this one? thinking about mobile clients that still send legacy headers.

alex: sticky-shard fallback. we want deterministic sticky behavior so mobile clients that lose a header still hit a compatible instance. fallback rules in the rollout config: shard_priority=sticky then header.

marta: adding a request — can we add a temporary tenant-exclusion list for customers that opted into strict v1 compatibility? i'd rather exclude them from the 10% canary than pin after the fact.

alex: yes — create an exclusion in the deploybot pinlist now if you have tenant ids. otherwise i'll backfill from the last compatibility report.

ken: shared the list in #support-ops. i put 5 tenants (T-233, T-454, T-712). they should be excluded from canary.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout v2:/generate -> eu-west - groups: 10%, 25%, 50% - start_time=1758011999 - operator=alex - exclusions=3 tenants - canary_policy=sticky-shard-fallback

priya: what are the rollback triggers for the canary window? we had a memory spike in a previous rollout where 2nd-stage autoscale didn't kick.

alex: rollback triggers: 1) client-error-rate (5xx) >= 1% for 10m; 2) request latency p95 increase > 120% baseline for 5m; 3) memory OOMs on >2 hosts in shard set; 4) abnormal KV-cache miss rate > 40% sustained for 10m. ops-bot will page on triggers.

ops-bot: alert config applied — will page on the above triggers to #eng-oncall and oncall@pagerduty.

marta: we should also gate by quality regression on our golden prompt set. canary traffic will run eval hooks and post delta to /internal/evals. if rouge reg > 0.03 we'll pause.

alex: good call — enabling golden-prompt eval hook (sampling 0.1% of canary traffic) and metric threshold set to 0.03.

ken: quick sanity check — are we doing quantized model variant in eu-west for this rollout? that affects latency baselines.

alex: yes, eu-west will use q4_0 variant. baseline metrics on that variant were attached in the deploy ticket. expecting p95 ~130ms.

priya: leaving a note: release notes need a short blurb about sticky-shard fallback and excluded tenants list + ops contact. i'll draft and attach to the ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy started (group 10%) at 1758011999. live instances: 12 shards (q4_0), exclusions applied.

marta: first telemetry coming in — p95 looks stable at 128ms, 5xx = 0.05% for now, golden-prompt delta = 0.01. nothing to flag yet.

ops-bot: autoscale observation: one host reached 85% memory, autoscale launched +1. no OOMs.

priya: i'm going to hold off marketing release note publish until we hit stage 25%. want to confirm no regressions.

alex: agreed. i'll wait for the next 30m window and then shift to 25% if metrics stay green.

deploy-bot: group shift to 25% completed at 1758012799. current p95=135ms, 5xx=0.08%, golden-prompt delta=0.015.

marta: slight uptick in p95 but within threshold. continuing to monitor.

ken: small question — if a tenant sees bad behavior, is the fastest path pinning them back to v1 or adding them to exclusions? which is faster?

alex: immediate mitigation is to add to exclusions (takes effect within ~30s) — pinning is heavier and requires SDK rollbacks for some clients. exclusions are preferred for quick safety net.

priya: noted. adding procedure to release notes.

deploy-bot: canary at 25% -> monitoring. next auto-shift scheduled in 25m. operator: alex.

marta: if anything spikes, i'm ready to trigger rollback. tagging @alex @priya. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks team. will post a final confirmation once we hit 50% or an incident if not.

deploy-bot: final note: if rollback is triggered, rollback playbook will revert routing to v1 and disable sticky-shard fallback for the rollout until manual re-enable.
